claim: Seal-first blinded external validation of a frozen early-season G+E_T1 system on the public 2024 G2F release.
The 2024 evaluation was calendar-time prospective before outcomes became public.
The 2022 420-cell primary cohort completed and failed calibration.
The 2022 available-case cohort supplied negative diagnostic evidence for interval transport.
The 2023 target season was unevaluable under the fixed T1 information interface without inventing a planting-date proxy.
The 2024 source-compatibility gate admitted a frozen 798-cell prediction universe before repository outcome access.
The 2024 primary observable sealed-key cohort contains 779 cells across 19 environments and 92 genotypes.
On the 2024 primary cohort the frozen G+E_T1 point predictor achieved RMSE 2.6197348509 and R2 0.1484401927.
The frozen B11 90% interval rule passed the inherited 2024 calibration criterion with environment-balanced coverage 0.8997721030.
The one-sided carry-forward widening rule failed the inherited 2024 calibration criterion with environment-balanced coverage 0.9521031534 and a worse mean interval score than the frozen control.
Case Study B establishes a general monotone or nonmonotone law of seasonal calibration error.
The direction of the previous observed calibration error was not sufficiently transport-stable to justify the predeclared one-sided next-season correction in this frozen sequence.
The 2024 postoutcome diagnostic shows mixed error structure including environment offsets, within-environment error, weak-to-moderate genotype ordering and prediction under-dispersion.
The postoutcome error decomposition is a new methodology.
For the deployed additive G+E architecture the environmental main effect cancels from same-environment genotype contrasts in exact arithmetic.
The additive-architecture audit establishes a new contraction theorem.
Case Study B validates support-based abstention as a selective-risk mechanism.
Case Study B introduces a new state-of-the-art GxE predictive architecture.
The closed T2 adaptive branch may be reopened using the same revealed evidence.
Case Study B is scientifically closed with external-validation contribution supported and predictive-method novelty not supported.
